LESSON: WRITING 7.4.1 SPELLING

Grade: SNE  /  hearing-impairment / Grade one
Subject: General
Strand: Strand 7
Topic 7.4: Writing 7.4.1 Spelling
Suggested lessons in curriculum: 2

SECTION 1: INTRODUCTION

This lesson covers Writing 7.4.1 Spelling, part of Strand 7 in SNE  /  hearing-impairment / Grade one General.

Key inquiry question: Why should people write neatly? 2. How can we spell words correctly?

You will study the official KICD learning outcomes, classroom activities, values, and competencies for this topic. Use Kenyan examples from your county, school, and community throughout.

SECTION 2: LEARNING OUTCOMES

By the end of this topic, you should be able to:

Refer to the KICD curriculum reference at the end of this lesson for the full list of outcomes.

SECTION 3: KEY CONCEPTS AND EXPLANATION

SECTION 4: LEARNING ACTIVITIES

A. At school

Follow your teacher’s guidance for group work, discussion, and practice on this topic.

B. At home with your parent or guardian

1. Read this lesson on Writing 7.4.1 Spelling together.
2. Discuss the key inquiry question and give examples from your area.
3. Write five sentences summarising what you learned.
4. Prepare for the revision quiz at the end of this topic.

SECTION 5: CORE COMPETENCIES, VALUES, AND PCIs

Core Competencies to be developed:
Learning to learn: The learner learns independently as they individually work on their own to match vocabulary learnt to pictures and objects for peer

review.

Values:
Unity: cooperation is nurtured as the learner appreciates other’s opinions in group work activities.

Responsibility: self-drive is developed as the learner works in groups to match vocabulary learnt to pictures and objects.

Link to

Pertinent and Contemporary Issues:
Life skills: Self-awareness is nurtured as the learner develops knowledge about the parts of their body.

Link to other Learning Areas:

Learner is able to relate the knowledge of parts of the body to Environmental activities

Suggested Learning Resources:

Manual alphabet chart, flash cards, internet, posters, online dictionaries, assistive devices fitted with appropriate technologies such as hearing aids and

amplifiers, adapted course books, flash cards, sign language dictionary, internet, signed audio-visual recordings
